key_insight: LLM prompting achieved the highest reported F1 for detecting caregiver burden in clinical transcripts, modestly exceeding weak supervision and an always-positive baseline.
clinical_relevance: Transcript-based burden detection could help identify dementia caregivers needing support, but these methods are not yet established for clinical deployment.
method: Analyzed de-identified caregiver–clinician transcripts from the COPE in PACE study using Zarit burden scores.
Compared an always-positive baseline, LLM prompting without fine-tuning, and weak supervision.
Also evaluated fully supervised sentence-level classification with only 1.1% burden-positive sentences.
evidence_signal: Precision/F1 were 0.40/0.57 for the baseline, 0.43/0.60 for LLM prompting, and 0.48/0.58 for weak supervision; supervised results of 0.19/0.25 used different labels and analysis units and are not directly comparable.
watch_item: Modest performance and severe sentence-level class imbalance highlight the need for larger annotated datasets and refined labeling before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Comparing Machine Learning Methods for Detecting Caregiver Burden in Transcribed Conversations with Clinicians
